changed.title: The 5 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 32435687 (the crown with one cell removed) has an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 9 gates on the promise
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 9 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun (u : Fin 5) (v : Fin 5) => (32435687 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) C
changed.unlocks: whether one named graph breaks the open pair's line with NOT gates
changed.context: A search. We hold a circuit with NOT gates of 11: one NOT over a circuit for the complement, which costs 10 on paper; that move cannot do better. What a circuit of 9 with NOT gates decides: with no AND/OR circuit of 14 it breaks the open pair at n = 5 (a saving of 15 - 9 = 6 against a bar of 5); with one, the graph is on the line. The floor with NOT gates we hold is 8 (a checked row). We hold no circuit of 9 gates with NOT gates; this is a search.

changed.title: Cyclic binary window tables simulate permutation programs with a unique indexed word on acceptance
changed.statement:
∀ (d m t : ℕ),
  let w := d + 1
  let State := Fin w → Bool
  let blockLen := w * (2 * d + 1)
  let n := t * blockLen + w
  let hb : 0 < blockLen := by dsimp [blockLen, w]; positivity
  let hn : 0 < n := by dsimp [n, w]; positivity
  ∀ (query : Fin t → Fin m) (step : Fin t → Bool → Equiv.Perm State)
    (start finish : State),
    let Pattern := Fin (w + 1) → Bool
    ∃ (block : Fin t → Bool → Fin blockLen → Pattern → Bool)
      (pin : Fin w → Pattern → Bool),
      ∀ x : Fin m → Bool,
        let row := fun (i : Fin n) =>
          if h : i.val / blockLen < t then
            let instr : Fin t := ⟨i.val / blockLen, h⟩
            block instr (x (query instr)) ⟨i.val % blockLen, Nat.mod_lt _ hb⟩
          else
            pin (Fin.ofNat (d + 1) (i.val - t * blockLen))
        let ok := fun (word : Fin n → Bool) => ∀ j : Fin n,
          row j (fun k => word ⟨(j.val + k.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩) = true
        let lastState := (List.finRange t).foldl (fun a s => step s (x (query s)) a) start
        (Finset.univ.filter ok).card = if lastState = finish then 1 else 0
changed.unlocks: encodes permutation branching programs by cyclic tests while preserving the number of accepting words
changed.context: Route each chosen permutation through 2w-1 layers of switches on coordinate pairs. For the induction, pair inputs and outputs on coordinate zero. Permutation edges form a degree-two bipartite multigraph on pairs. Color cycles alternately, sending one of each color through each pair. Recurse inside each color. Each switch layer takes w shifts: copy each dropped bit except on the chosen coordinate, where the other bits determine whether to flip. In the final w shifts require the dropped target bits and append start bits. Closure then selects one run.

changed.title: A balanced product gives a monotone depth bound for deciding arbitrary cyclic window tables
changed.statement:
∀ (n w : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n),
  let I := n * 2 ^ (w + 1)
  ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack I C ∧ C.output < I + C.size ∧
    C.size ≤ 6 * n * 8 ^ w + 3 ∧
    C.depth I ≤ 1 + (Nat.log2 n + 1) * (w + 1) + w ∧
    ∀ table : Fin n → (Fin (w + 1) → Bool) → Bool,
      let x := (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => List.ofFn (fun p : Fin (2 ^ (w + 1)) =>
        table i (fun j => p.val.testBit j.val)))).flatten
      C.eval x = true ↔ ∃ word : Fin n → Bool, ∀ i : Fin n,
        table i (fun j => word ⟨(i.val + j.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩) = true
changed.unlocks: gives a parallel table decision circuit of bounded depth and size at each width
changed.context: At each position form the Boolean transition matrix on w-bit windows, using either appended bit. With w=0 OR both input bits in the single cell. Pad the list with identity matrices to a power of two and multiply in a balanced tree. Each product uses one AND layer and w binary OR layers per entry. OR its diagonal to test for a permitted path returning to its initial window. The closure gives an indexed cyclic word even when w exceeds n. Count gates and longest paths in the same list. Gate-price companions cannot exist for this constructive ceiling.

changed.title: Exact prefix counts and output pivots for a stopped three-state cyclic scan
changed.statement:
∀ (k r d i : Nat), 6 ≤ r → k + 3 + d = 5 * r →
  let attempts := r - 5
  d ≤ attempts → i < k → i + (2 * attempts - d) ≤ k →
  ∀ constant : Nat → Fin (2 ^ k),
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc cell =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit cell)
        (!(word.testBit ((cell + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((cell + 2) % k))).toNat <<< cell)) 0
  let state := fun (row rounds key : Nat) =>
    (List.range rounds).foldl (fun prev tick =>
      step (prev ^^^ rot 1 prev ^^^ rot (k - 1) prev) ^^^ rot (2 * tick) key ^^^
        (constant (tick + 1)).val) (rot 1 key ^^^ row)
  let injected := fun (round key pos : Nat) =>
    xor ((rot (2 * (round - 1)) key).testBit (pos % k))
      ((constant round).val.testBit (pos % k))
  let bit := fun (row round key pos : Nat) => (state row round key).testBit (pos % k)
  let guard := fun (row round key stop : Nat) =>
    xor (xor (bit row round key (stop - 2)) (bit row round key (stop - 1))) (bit row round key stop)
  let move := fun (mode letter : Nat) =>
    let aligned := ((mode == 1) && letter.testBit 0 && letter.testBit 1) ||
      ((mode == 2) && letter.testBit 1)
    let hit := letter.testBit 2
    (if aligned then (if hit then 0 else 2) else 1,
      hit.toNat + (aligned && hit).toNat)
  let summary := fun (code length : Nat) =>
    (List.range length).foldl (fun (st : Nat × Nat) digitPos =>
      let result := move st.1 ((code >>> (3 * digitPos)) % 8)
      (result.1, st.2 + result.2)) (0, 0)
  let q := k + i + 3 * r - d
  let trace := fun (row key length : Nat) =>
    ((List.range length).foldl (fun (st : Nat × Nat × Nat) idx =>
      let t := 5 + idx
      let edge := q - 13 - 3 * idx + st.2.1
      let left := edge + 3 - 2 * t
      let x := rot 1 key ^^^ row
      let v := injected (t - 1) key (edge + 2)
      let oldMix := guard row (t - 2) key (edge + 2)
      let uBit := xor oldMix (injected (t - 1) key (edge + 1))
      let one := if st.1 == 1 then
        bit row (t - 1) key edge == !(xor uBit v)
        else x.testBit ((left + 2) % k)
      let two := if st.1 == 0 then x.testBit ((left + 1) % k)
        else bit row (t - 1) key (edge - 1) == v
      let hit := guard row (t - 1) key edge
      let digit := one.toNat + 2 * two.toNat + 4 * hit.toNat
      let outcome := move st.1 digit
      (outcome.1, st.2.1 + outcome.2, st.2.2 ||| (digit <<< (3 * idx)))) (0, 0, 0)).2.2
  ∀ (a : Nat) (code : Fin (8 ^ a)), a ≤ attempts →
    (a = 0 ∨ d < (summary code.val (a - 1)).2 + 2 * (attempts + 1 - a)) →
    ∀ rowName : Fin (2 ^ k),
    let keys := (List.range (2 ^ k)).filter (fun raw => trace rowName.val raw a == code.val)
    keys.length = 2 ^ (k - 3 * a) ∧
      (a = attempts →
        let m := (summary code.val a).2 - d
        ∀ (key₁ key₂ : Fin (2 ^ k)) (j : Fin m),
          trace rowName.val key₁.val a = code.val → trace rowName.val key₂.val a = code.val →
          let x₁ := rot 1 key₁.val ^^^ rowName.val
          let x₂ := rot 1 key₂.val ^^^ rowName.val
          (∀ p : Fin k, (∀ b : Nat, b ≤ j.val → (q + b) % k ≠ p.val) →
            x₁.testBit p.val = x₂.testBit p.val) →
          xor ((state rowName.val r key₁.val).testBit (i + j.val))
              ((state rowName.val r key₂.val).testBit (i + j.val)) =
            xor (x₁.testBit ((q + j.val) % k)) (x₂.testBit ((q + j.val) % k)))
changed.unlocks: identifies the free starting bits and the terminal output pivots used in the three-state row decoder
changed.context: An aligned hit removes the nonlinear term at a second position. An aligned miss fixes the second bit beyond the next edge. Every unaligned step excludes one adjacent pair. Cut the integer lift of the starting word off on the right. In each live round solve the three fresh pivots L+2,L+1,L in that order. The pivots miss the eventual hidden block, leaving k-3a free bits for a length-a prefix. Compare two keys differing only on a hidden prefix through the penultimate round. Only the final key addition can change the selected output.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 6 bipartite graph with mask 275444 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 11 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 6) => (275444 : ℕ).testBit (6 * u.val + v.val)) 11
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 6 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 12 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out, equal gates merged and unread gates dropped); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 11; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 9 (on paper), a gap of 3. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 9 right, gate j writes wire 10 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 24 inputs with one vertex on each side.
